sources.title: The Theta-Gamma Neural Code
sources.access_method: PMC open access full text read
sources.key_contribution: Canonical review establishing theta-gamma neural code framework; theta oscillation as multi-item multiplexing clock; theta/gamma frequency ratio determines WM capacity
sources.notes: Theoretical review synthesizing ~20 years of evidence; original Lisman-Idiart 1995 model validated with updated evidence

sources.title: Cross-frequency coupling supports multi-item working memory in the human hippocampus
sources.authors: Axmacher N, Henseler MM, Jensen O, Weinreich I, Elger CE, Fell J
sources.access_method: PMC open access full text read
sources.key_contribution: Human intracranial EEG: theta frequency decreases with memory load (7.50→6.43 Hz), theta/gamma ratio ~4:1 constant; modulation width (not amplitude) predicts WM performance (R=0.68)
sources.notes: n=14 epilepsy patients; Sternberg task with 1/2/4 novel faces; direct human validation of Lisman-Idiart model

sources.title: Control of working memory by phase-amplitude coupling of human hippocampal neurons
sources.authors: Daume J, Kamiński J, Schjetnan AGP, Salimpour Y, Khan U, Kyzar M, Reed CM, Anderson WS, Valiante TA, Mamelak AN, Rutishauser U
sources.access_method: PMC open access full text read
sources.key_contribution: Single-neuron: hippocampal PAC neurons (~37%) distinct from content neurons (~25%); PAC neurons generate information-enhancing noise correlations; vmPFC theta synchrony with PAC neurons predicts RT (p=6e-5)
sources.notes: n=36 neurosurgical patients; Behnke-Fried hybrid electrodes; counterintuitive finding: PAC strength higher at load 1 than load 3

sources.title: Frequency of gamma oscillations routes flow of information in the hippocampus
sources.authors: Colgin LL, Denninger T, Fyhn M, Hafting T, Bonnevie T, Jensen O, Moser MB, Moser EI
sources.key_contribution: CA1 has fast gamma (65-100 Hz, MEC input, sensory) and slow gamma (25-55 Hz, CA3 input, memory); segregated by theta phase
sources.notes: Rat CA1 LFP; dual-channel routing via theta phase is mechanistically important; not open access

sources.title: High gamma power is phase-locked to theta oscillations in human neocortex
sources.authors: Canolty RT, Edwards E, Dalal SS, Soltani M, Nagarajan SS, Kirsch HE, Berger MS, Barbaro NM, Knight RT
sources.key_contribution: First systematic demonstration of theta-gamma PAC across human neocortex using ECoG; different tasks produce different spatial PAC patterns
sources.notes: Human ECoG from neurosurgical patients; established theta (4-8 Hz) modulates high gamma (80-150 Hz); not open access

sources.title: Hippocampal-prefrontal theta-gamma coupling during performance of a spatial working memory task
sources.authors: Tamura M, Spellman TJ, Rosen AM, Gogos JA, Gordon JA
sources.key_contribution: Mouse HPC-mPFC theta-slow-gamma coupling compensatory enhancement with task difficulty; predicts correct performance; cross-regional WM coordination
sources.notes: Mouse spatial WM; Nat Commun - likely open access but not directly retrieved

sources.title: Cell-type-specific contributions to theta-gamma coupled rhythms in the hippocampus
sources.authors: Sengupta S, Talidou A, Lefebvre J, Skinner FK
sources.key_contribution: CCK basket cells initiate coupled rhythms and regularize theta; PV basket cells enhance both theta and gamma amplitudes - first systematic dissection of cell-type contributions
sources.notes: Computational model with experimental constraints; predictions testable with optogenetics

sources.title: Spectral dependence as a framework for neural coordination
sources.authors: Besosa C, Qin Y, Burke SN, Maurer AP
sources.key_contribution: Challenges traditional spectral parcellation: gamma power covaries with theta power; CFC may emerge from shared circuit energy dissipation constraints rather than dedicated mechanisms
sources.notes: Challenges framework paper; registered as contested claim C-2026-09-17-01; important minority view

sources.title: Theta-gamma coupling and working memory deficits in schizophrenia
sources.key_contribution: SCZ patients show reduced theta-gamma coupling positively correlated with WM performance; coupling deficits precede WM deficits
sources.notes: Already registered in source_registry; included as disease relevance anchor

coverage_assessment.notes: Meets all requirements: ≥5 sources ✓, ≥2 open full text ✓, ≥1 official institutional source ✓. Synthesizes rodent mechanistic + human electrophysiology + human single-neuron + computational modeling.
